newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Ramos urges calm over peso plunge.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos urges calm over peso plunge.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos on Sunday appealed to Filipinos not to panic after the Central Bank effectively devalued the peso and said he expected the situation to normalise in a few days.
"Let's just let things settle down," Ramos told reporters. "I am appealing to all our people not to be suddenly traumatised by these actions of the Central Bank," he added.
Ramos praised the Central Bank for picking last Friday to announce its decision to let the the peso trade in a wider band.
"So there is this weekend during which the markets, both the financial and the stock exchange, will calm down, settle down and normalise," he said.

Ramos said before the peso move was announced, the government alerted local officials so there would be "no sudden excitement ...that would raise prices because this one will normalise in a few days."
Ramos insisted the Central Bank move was not a devaluation.
"It's just the (Central Bank) getting out as a market player. It is in fact not just a player, it is a market leader by not intervening anymore in the buying and selling of dollars."
Ramos added: "That's the situation as far as I see it and, believe me, I know the situation."
The peso plunged 11.5 percent to 29.45 per dollar in the initial hours of currency trading on Friday forcing suspension of the trading. Trading will resume on Monday.
